intent.goal: Let verify.py emit its verdict as a coordinator-signed transcript and let run_report.py require one against the committed public key, so a tier advance costs a verdict the worker could not have typed (#281, the #386 prerequisite) — with the unsigned path byte-identical until the maintainer commits .orca/dispatch-pubkey.
intent.ruled_out: Committing a pubkey from this session (coordinator answer Q1=c: the seed never originates in an agent session); a second key scheme or any new crypto (ed25519.py + the dispatch envelope are reused, verify.py mirrors canonical form with a parity test as _canonical_dispatch does); reading the pubkey from the working tree in run_report.py (would turn both existing self-run reports RED and demote two missions — out of scope; the key is read at each report's own inventory_at instead, coordinator answer Q2); any Rekor/network path (U-SIG-2); reshaping existing verify.py checks; removing an existing verify.py name to hold the RV-D2 width pin at 90 (the pin moved to 91 with its reason, coordinator answer 'a').
intent.why: verify-gate.sh already discovers .orca/dispatch-pubkey and passes --dispatch-pubkey, so committing the key is one switch for two enforcements; the doc and the dormancy pin now say so, so the maintainer flips it consciously. Reading the key AT the report's pin is what keeps history consistent: pre-key reports keep today's path, post-key reports require a verified transcript, and a new run cannot dodge by pinning an old commit because its own artifacts must exist there.
